setup.zh: 你浮上水面的时候，日头已经落尽了。那口鼎跟着你浮了上来，越浮越小，落在你手心里，沉甸甸的，暖的。
setup.en: By the time you surface, the sun has set. The cauldron rises with you, smaller and smaller, and lands in your palm, heavy and warm.

recap.zh: 第一鼎归来，木牌亮了第二条尾巴；柳树底下站着一个白衣人：「太一宫，赵昂。」「因为天下，该归于一。」他看见了你掌心的印：「烙上了，就是宫里的。」
recap.en: The first cauldron came home and a second tail lit on the token; under the willow stood a man in white: "Taiyi Palace. Zhao Ang." "Because all under heaven should be one." He saw the mark in your palm: "Burned in, it is the Palace's."

zh: 木牌上，第二条尾巴亮了。
en: A cauldron the size of a palm, warm.
On the token, a second tail alight.
Under the willow, someone in white.

story.zh:
小满浮上水面的时候，日头已经落尽了，天边只剩一抹暗红。那口鼎跟着他浮了上来，越浮越小，浮出水面时只有巴掌大，落在他手心里，沉甸甸的，暖的。

胸口的木牌烫得前所未有，他低头一看，木牌上那只蜷着的小狐狸，九条尾巴里，第二条亮了。
story.en:
When Xiaoman surfaced, the sun had set, with only a streak of dark red left at the sky's edge. The cauldron rose with him, growing smaller, and when it broke the surface it was the size of a palm; it landed in his hand, heavy and warm.

The token at his chest burned as never before; he looked down, and of the nine tails of the little curled fox on it, a second was alight.

exits.means: takes up the cauldron, keeps it, faces the stranger in white

story.zh:
那人站在岸边一株老柳树底下，一身白衣，腰悬长剑，正是方才上游柳树底下那一个。

他的目光，落在小满手心里那口巴掌大的鼎上，开口第一句话，却是：「多谢。」

小满一怔：「谢什么？」那人道：「二十五年，宫里请不动他。你一个上午，就把他请上来了。」他往前走了两步，月光照在他腰间那柄剑的剑鞘上，剑鞘头上刻着一个记号：一个圆圈，圈里一横。「太一宫，赵昂。」

太一宫，这三个字小满听过不止一回；从宫里的人自己嘴里报出来，这是头一回。眼前这一个，脚下没声，是筑了基的；听那口气，不是跑腿的。

小满攥紧了手里的鼎，道：「你们拿姑娘砸了他二十五年。二十五个姑娘。今天城楼底下，还压死了一个卖豆腐的。」

赵昂的眉头动了一动。那一下极快，快得小满几乎以为是月光晃的。他的眼睛往城西水门那边偏了一偏，又收了回来。他道：「……二十五个。」隔了一会儿，又道：「宫里有一位执事，每年入秋到这城里来，住到十月十八，来了二十五年。我只来了半个月。他是怎么办的差，我没问。」他说完这一句，脸上便又什么都没有了，目光重新落回那口鼎上，道：「这东西，该归太一宫。」

小满道：「为什么？」

赵昂这才正眼看了他，道：「因为天下，该归于一。」

小满怀里的银月，猛地一颤。

「在九天之上。」银月一字一字地道，「那道光劈下来的时候，光里那个声音，说的就是这一句：天下，该归于一。」

赵昂看不见银月，也听不见它说话，他只看见小满抱着一团湿衣裳，脸色一下子变了。他的手，慢慢地按上了剑柄。

他的眼睛往下一落，落在小满托着鼎的那只手上。鼎底下，掌心里，那个印露了出来。赵昂看着它，看了很久，脸上第一回有了一点东西，说不清是惊，还是别的什么。他道：「宫里的印。」顿了一顿，「烙上了，就是宫里的。」

小满把手一翻，掌心朝下，扣在了鼎上。他道：「黑松岭，有一个孩子，十岁上下，摔断了腰，死在崖根底下。他领口里缝着一锭银子，底下也錾着这个。」他看着赵昂，「锁儿。是你们的人么？」

赵昂没有答。月光底下，他那张好看的脸，一点一点地白了下去。过了很久，他才道：「……宫里的孩子，没有名字。」

小满没有再问。他听明白了：锁儿在宫里，没有名字；说这话的人，大约也是宫里的孩子。

赵昂盯着他，按在剑柄上的手松了又紧，终于放了下来，道：「今日冰夷护着你。我不跟一条河打架。」他转过身去，走了两步，又停住，头也不回地道：「这东西，你拿不稳的。」说罢，一步一步走进了柳树后面的黑地里，脚下没有一点声息。

小满站在河边，把这几年里见过的那个记号，一个一个摆在心里：锁儿领口里那一锭，开山门那天山脚下塞进一个哭着的爹手里的那一锭，三老匣子里那一锭，腊八那面镜子烙进他掌心里的这一个，赵昂剑鞘头上那一个。买孩子的，是它；拿孩子去换白狐狸的，是它；拿姑娘砸了冰夷二十五年的，是它。劈断银月尾巴的那道光里，说的也是它：一。

天下，该归于一。他从前只当这是一句好听的话。
story.en:
The man stood under an old willow at the water's edge, all in white, a long sword at his waist — the same one who had stood under the willows upstream.

His eyes fell on the palm-sized cauldron in Xiaoman's hand, and the first thing he said was: "Thank you."

Xiaoman was startled: "For what?" The man said: "For twenty-five years the Palace couldn't get him to come up. You did it in one morning." He took two steps forward; moonlight fell on the scabbard at his waist, and on its tip was a mark: a circle, with one bar inside it. "Taiyi Palace. Zhao Ang."

Taiyi Palace — Xiaoman had heard the name more than once; this was the first time one of its own people had said it aloud. This one walked without a sound and had laid his Foundation; by his tone, he was no errand boy.

Xiaoman gripped the cauldron in his hand: "You battered him with girls for twenty-five years. Twenty-five girls. And today a tofu-seller was crushed under the tower."

Zhao Ang's brows moved — so quickly Xiaoman almost thought it was the moonlight shifting. His eyes slid toward the water gate on the west side and came back. He said: "…Twenty-five." After a while: "There is a steward of the Palace who comes to this city every autumn and stays until the eighteenth of the tenth month. Twenty-five years he has come. I have been here half a month. How he does his work, I didn't ask." With that his face was empty again; his eyes went back to the cauldron: "This belongs to the Taiyi Palace."

Xiaoman said: "Why?"

Only then did Zhao Ang really look at him: "Because all under heaven should be one."

Yinyue, in Xiaoman's arms, gave a violent start.

"High in the ninth heaven," Yinyue said, word by word. "When that light struck down, the voice in the light said exactly this: all under heaven should be one."

Zhao Ang could not see Yinyue nor hear her speak; he saw only Xiaoman clutching a bundle of wet clothes, his face suddenly changed. His hand slowly came to rest on his sword hilt.

His eyes dropped to the hand that held the cauldron. Under the cauldron, in the palm, the brand showed. Zhao Ang looked at it a long time, and for the first time something showed in his face — surprise, or something else. He said: "The Palace's seal." A pause. "Burned in, it is the Palace's."

Xiaoman turned his hand over, palm down, over the cauldron. He said: "On Black Pine Ridge there was a child, ten or so, who broke his back and died at the foot of a cliff. He had an ingot of silver sewn in his collar, with this on its base too." He looked at Zhao Ang. "Suo'er. Was he one of yours?"

Zhao Ang did not answer. In the moonlight his handsome face slowly went white. After a long while he said: "…The Palace's children have no names."

Xiaoman asked no more. He understood: in the Palace, Suo'er had no name; and the one saying so was, most likely, a Palace child himself.

Zhao Ang stared at him, his hand on the hilt tightening and loosening, and at last he let it go: "Today Bingyi guards you. I don't fight a river." He turned away, took two steps, stopped, and said without looking back: "You won't be able to hold on to that." Then, step by step, he walked into the dark behind the willows, without a sound underfoot.

Xiaoman stood by the river and laid out in his mind, one by one, every time he had seen that mark these past years: the ingot in Suo'er's collar; the ingot pressed into a weeping father's hand at the foot of the mountain the day the gate opened; the ingot in the Three Elders' casket; this one the mirror burned into his palm at Laba; the one on the tip of Zhao Ang's scabbard. What bought children was it; what sent children to trade for a white fox was it; what battered Bingyi with girls for twenty-five years was it. And in the light that cut off Yinyue's tails, what the voice said was it too: one.

All under heaven should be one. He had once taken it for a fine-sounding phrase.

exits.means: hesitates, asks what will happen, wants to wait

text.zh: 它在你掌心里，一明，一暗，像在很慢地呼吸。
text.en: It lies in your palm, light and dark, as if breathing very slowly.
